"checked-record": "Pass only payload fields: Interval {lo, hi}, Triple {data} for Sized 3, and Percent {value} for Bounded 0 101. Input constructors validate cross-field predicates or normalize values inside Lean without changing caller input. Results expose payload fields, not proofs. A standalone result-only package works without any checked input. The tested Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as ordinary GMP integers in C and cpp_int values in C++. The generated adapter applies the exact constructor selected for Packet and its nested Word field through direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value branch. C callers initialize and clear generated records and owning results; C++ callers use Packet values, vectors, optionals, products, results, Holder and Choice. Rejected inputs leave the complete caller graph and existing C output unchanged, and later valid calls recover. Array and Option results contain proof-free Packet payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call."

The selected Lean constructor checks each input and may normalize it; rejection identifies the parameter and constructor and preserves caller data. Results contain copied payload fields with proofs erased. Both ordinary and independently reviewed packages, including standalone result-only packages, passed installed checks. The tested Rust Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as num_bigint::BigUint values. Holder nests Packet, and Choice::Packet carries it in the active Choice branch. Generated Rust adapters apply the exact Packet and nested Word constructors selected at each direct, repeated, Array, List, Option, tuple, Result, Holder and Choice input site. Rejected calls preserve the complete caller graph and later valid calls recover. Packet arrays and options returned by Lean contain proof-free payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata."

edits.previous: "note": "Generated host records carry typed runtime payloads without proof values. Additional nested JVM acceptance: Two independent author builds reproduce the complete Maven package. Author sources are removed before offline installation; Java and Kotlin callers replay after moving the installed tree and execute again after deleting all consumer sources, giving six executions per selection. Compiler probes check the generated API, Java and Kotlin Unit classes, Kotlin function references and result nullability. The full API checks direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, both Except branches, Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value field, including exact per-site constructors, normalization, complete rejected-input snapshots and recovery. Independent controls reject every missing or changed retained record and coordinated resource, model, package, probe and execution mutations. Checked-record JVM acceptance covers the established top-level Interval, Sized 3 and Bounded 0 101 forms plus the tested acyclic Packet, Holder and Choice forms through Array, List, Option, Product and Except copied positions. Generic and recursive records, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Both author routes and full/result-only APIs reproduce complete Maven packages from two author roots, remove author sources, install offline, replay after relocation and execute again after deleting all consumer sources. The runs use JDK 22.0.2, Kotlin 2.2.0 and Lean 4.32.2 on Linux x64/glibc 2.36 with an explicit 2.36 package floor and 64-bit machine words. Original receipts, retained package members, compiler probes, execution records and selected sources are archived; native libraries and the closed JAR retain exact identities without copied bytes. Constructor entry counts and peak memory are unmeasured. Hosted glibc 2.38 release-floor acceptance remains assigned to the recurring workflow. Additional inherited jvm acceptance: The jvm installed lane authenticates the ordinary full inherited checked-record package selection for java, kotlin. The full API checks valid, normalized, invalid parent, invalid child, alias, nested Fin, repeated-constructor and recovery cases before projecting proof-free results. Two independent author builds, source removal, offline installation, relocation and unchanged caller replay are retained where the host permits them. The fixture covers inherited parent subobjects, child checked fields, aliases, nested inheritance, repeated constructor selections, and constructor-free results. Ordinary and independently reviewed sources are exercised in full and result-only Maven packages through independent Java and Kotlin callers. Complete Maven packages are reproduced, installed offline, executed before and after relocation, and reduced to source-free runtime deployments. Complete package archives, receipts, inventories, probes, execution records, TAP, controls, and producer/checker/archive source closures are retained. The package floor is glibc 2.38; the archive records and verifies the hosted runner's independently observed glibc and JVM tool identities. Compiler, operating-system, JDK, Kotlin compiler, Maven-format archive, and glibc distributions remain trusted inputs. This archive establishes installed JVM behavior, not promotion into the public support inventory. Inherited checked-record acceptance covers only the tested acyclic Span → Ticket → Stamped chain, its Ticket alias, repeated direct parameters, nested parent constraints and proof-free Ticket/Stamped results. Value-carrying receiver-dependent inherited fields, generic or recursive inheritance, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed."

Generic checked records, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. The component requires its packaged native Lean host and is not a standalone WASI command. edits.previous: "checked-record": "Pass generated record objects containing Math::BigInt values and plain array references, without proofs. Lean runs the selected constructor for each input; it may normalize accepted data, or reject with the parameter and constructor name while preserving caller values. Results contain independent copied payload fields with proofs erased. Ordinary and reviewed packages, including standalone result-only packages, passed installed checks. The tested Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as Math::BigInt values. Holder nests Packet, and Choice::Packet carries it in the active Choice branch. Generated Perl adapters apply the exact Packet and nested Word constructors selected at each direct, repeated, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder and Choice input site. Rejected calls preserve the complete caller graph and later valid calls recover. Packet arrays and options returned by Lean contain proof-free payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata."

edits.previous: "checked-record": "Pass only payload fields: Interval {lo, hi}, Triple {data} for Sized 3, and Percent {value} for Bounded 0 101, using bigint and bigint[] values. The selected Lean constructor checks or normalizes each input; constructor rejection identifies the parameter and constructor. Calls preserve complete caller inputs, and later valid calls recover. Results contain copied payloads without proofs. Ordinary and independently reviewed packages, including standalone result-only packages, passed Node, page, React and worker checks in all three browser engines. Packet is a proof-free object with digit: bigint for Fin 10 and word: bigint for a checked Nat Subtype. The selected adapter descends through Array, List, Option, Product, Except, enclosing Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value field, applies the exact constructor selected for every public site and nested Word field, and leaves the caller's complete rejected graph unchanged. Repeated parameters keep independent constructor choices; later valid calls recover. Copied Array and Option results contain the same nested payload objects without proof fields or input-constructor selection. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata."

Generated PHP-Wasm adapters apply the exact Packet and nested Word constructors selected at each direct, repeated, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder and Choice input site. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata."

edits.previous: "checked-record": "Pass generated record objects with only payload fields: Interval {lo, hi}, Triple {data} for Sized 3, and Percent {value} for Bounded 0 101. Nat payloads use Brick\\Math\\BigInteger, including small values; data is a consecutive-key array of BigInteger values. Lean runs the constructor selected for each parameter, including normalization. Rejection names the parameter and constructor, preserves complete caller inputs, and permits later valid calls. Results contain copied payloads without proofs. Ordinary, independently reviewed and standalone result-only packages passed weak/strict and startup/lazy Node/Chromium checks on wasm32 PHP 8.4.1. The tested PHP-Wasm Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as Brick\\Math\\BigInteger values. Holder nests Packet, and ChoicePacket carries it in the active Choice branch. Generated PHP-Wasm adapters apply the exact Packet and nested Word constructors selected at each direct, repeated, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder and Choice input site. Rejected calls preserve the complete caller graph and later valid calls recover. Packet arrays and options returned by Lean contain proof-free payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata."

edits.previous: "checked-record": "Pass generated record objects with only payload fields: Interval {lo, hi}, Triple {data} for Sized 3, and Percent {value} for Bounded 0 101. Ordinary, independently reviewed and standalone result-only packages passed weak/strict and startup/lazy Node/Chromium checks on wasm32 PHP 8.4.1. The tested PHP-Wasm Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as Brick\\Math\\BigInteger values. Holder nests Packet, and ChoicePacket carries it in the active Choice branch. Generated PHP-Wasm adapters apply the exact Packet and nested Word constructors selected at each direct, repeated, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder and Choice input site. Rejected calls preserve the complete caller graph and later valid calls recover. Packet arrays and options returned by Lean contain proof-free payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata."

edits.previous: "checked-record": "Pass only payload fields: Interval {lo, hi}, Triple {data} for Sized 3, and Percent {value} for Bounded 0 101, using bigint and bigint[] values. The selected Lean constructor checks or normalizes each input; constructor rejection identifies the parameter and constructor. Calls preserve complete caller inputs, and later valid calls recover. Results contain copied payloads without proofs. Ordinary and independently reviewed packages, including standalone result-only packages, passed Node, page, React and worker checks in all three browser engines. Packet is a proof-free object with digit: bigint for Fin 10 and word: bigint for a checked Nat Subtype. The selected adapter descends through Array, List, Option, Product, Except, enclosing Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value field, applies the exact constructor selected for every public site and nested Word field, and leaves the caller's complete rejected graph unchanged. Repeated parameters keep independent constructor choices; later valid calls recover. Copied Array and Option results contain the same nested payload objects without proof fields or input-constructor selection. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata."

The full API checks direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, both Except branches, Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value field, including exact per-site constructors, normalization, complete rejected-input snapshots and recovery. Independent controls reject every missing record and coordinated report, resource, model and package mutation. Nested checked-record C/C++ acceptance covers only the tested acyclic Packet, Holder and Choice forms through Array, List, Option, Product and Except copied positions. Generic records, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Both author routes and full/result-only APIs reproduce complete packages from two roots. Independent C11/GMP and C++20 callers install offline after author removal and replay after physical relocation on Linux x64/glibc 2.36 with an explicit 2.36 package floor. Constructor/source entry counts and peak memory are unmeasured. These local runs do not establish hosted or glibc 2.38 release-floor acceptance. Additional inherited native acceptance: The native installed lane authenticates the ordinary full inherited checked-record package selection for c, cpp. The full API checks valid, normalized, invalid parent, invalid child, alias, nested Fin, repeated-constructor and recovery cases before projecting proof-free results. Two independent author builds, source removal, offline installation, relocation and unchanged caller replay are retained where the host permits them. Hosted GitHub Linux x64 acceptance with an explicit glibc 2.38 package floor and load ceiling 12. Four ordinary/reviewed full/result-only selections reproduce complete C and C++ packages from two author roots, install offline after author removal, and replay unchanged independent C11/GMP and C++20 callers after physical relocation. Parent and child constructors, repeated positions with different constructor selections, nested inheritance, aliases and invalid inner and outer values are exercised; result-only packages erase input-constructor metadata. Complete original C and C++ archives, receipts, caller sources, execution records, the original TAP, the hosted verification and the exact producer source closure are retained. External compiler and operating-system distributions are not retained. Other hosts, callbacks and owned positions require separate evidence. This archive does not itself promote support. Inherited checked-record acceptance covers only the tested acyclic Span → Ticket → Stamped chain, its Ticket alias, repeated direct parameters, nested parent constraints and proof-free Ticket/Stamped results. Value-carrying receiver-dependent inherited fields, generic or recursive inheritance, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Additional recursive native acceptance: The native installed lane authenticates the ordinary mutual recursive checked-record selection for c, cpp. Original inputs, exact failures, preserved rejected values, recovery and proof-free results are retained; independently reproduced packages are installed without author sources and replayed after relocation where the host permits it. Hosted Ubuntu 24.04 Linux x64 acceptance records the observed glibc runtime and enforces a glibc 2.38 package floor; other operating systems and architectures remain separate requirements. Ordinary source and independently reviewed Binding IR routes reproduce complete C and C++ packages from two isolated author roots, remove author sources, install offline, relocate and replay without consumer sources or compilers. The immutable C and C++ callers cover mutual records and variants, aliases, arrays and options, active branches, exact Fin and Subtype diagnostics, malformed values, cycles, depth limits, preserved rejected inputs and recovery. Proof fields are erased, recursive nominal identities stay distinct, and results contain no runtime proof constructors. Callbacks, owned values, asynchronous calls, retained identity, dependent index kinds, open dependent records and zero-payload records remain separate requirements. Original package archives, receipts, models, source inputs, caller sources, reports, controls, TAP, checker output, toolchain log and exact producer, checker and archiver source closures are retained; external compiler and operating-system distributions remain trusted. Recursive checked-record acceptance covers the tested Packet self-cycle and Envelope ↔ Step mutual cycle, their aliases, Array/Option wrappers, active branches, Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields in copied parameters, results and fields. It does not establish generic recursive records, other recursive graph shapes, value-carrying receiver-dependent fields, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks or owned positions.",

edits.previous: "checked-record": "Pass only payload fields: Interval {lo, hi}, Triple {data} for Sized 3, and Percent {value} for Bounded 0 101. Input constructors validate cross-field predicates or normalize values inside Lean without changing caller input. Results expose payload fields, not proofs. A standalone result-only package works without any checked input. The tested Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as ordinary GMP integers in C and cpp_int values in C++. The generated adapter applies the exact constructor selected for Packet and its nested Word field through direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value branch. C callers initialize and clear generated records and owning results; C++ callers use Packet values, vectors, optionals, products, results, Holder and Choice. Rejected inputs leave the complete caller graph and existing C output unchanged, and later valid calls recover. Array and Option results contain proof-free Packet payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata."
